title: Fraction Word Problems and Estimates
short: Use 0, 1/2 and 1 to check whether an answer is reasonable.

blocks.html: Now that you can add and subtract any fractions and mixed numbers, it helps to know roughly what an answer should be before you work it out. The landmarks 0, $\frac{1}{2}$ and 1 make that quick.
Round each fraction to the nearest benchmark, 0, $\frac{1}{2}$ or 1, and work with those. An exact answer far from the estimate needs a second look.

Compare the numerator with the denominator. If the numerator is close to 0, the fraction is near 0. If it is close to half the denominator, the fraction is near $\frac{1}{2}$. If it is close to the denominator, the fraction is near 1. So $\frac{7}{8}$ is near 1 and $\frac{2}{5}$ is near $\frac{1}{2}$.

blocks.name: fractionline
blocks.cap: Move the point and compare it with $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{4}{8}$ on the line below. $\frac{5}{8}$ is just past one half.

blocks.title: Catch a mistake
steps: The sum must be more than $\frac{1}{2}$, since $\frac{1}{2}$ is one of the parts.
$\frac{3}{7}$ is less than $\frac{1}{2}$, because 3 is less than half of 7.
blocks.a: No. The sum is $\frac{9}{10}$, close to 1.

blocks.title: A story
blocks.q: Mia walks $\frac{2}{3}$ mile, then $\frac{3}{4}$ mile. How far does she walk?
steps: $1\frac{5}{12}$ is near $1\frac{1}{2}$, so it is reasonable.

blocks.html: Trusting an answer without checking its size. $\frac{2}{5} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{7}$ looks tidy, but it is smaller than one of the parts. A one-second benchmark check catches it.
